title: Detect agent questions in Stop hook
description:
The Stop hook question detection is implemented but not working. The hook (`extensions/claude/stop-hook.sh`) reads `last_assistant_message` from stdin, checks the last 500 chars for `?`, and should report `question` state. Instead it always reports `idle`.

## Symptoms

- Agent finishes a turn ending with a question mark
- Dashboard shows `idle` instead of `question`
- Stop hook fires but the `?` grep doesn't match

## Debugging

Debug logging added to stop-hook.sh — dumps raw input to `/tmp/claude-stop-hook-debug.json` and parsed message to `/tmp/claude-stop-hook-msg.txt`. Check these after the next Stop hook invocation to see what `last_assistant_message` actually contains.

## Possible causes

1. `last_assistant_message` field is empty or missing from the Stop hook JSON
2. The message is in a different format than expected (e.g. structured blocks, not plain text)
3. `jq` is not available or fails silently
4. The `?` is outside the last 500 chars (unlikely for short responses)

## Related

The Notification hook with `elicitation_dialog` matcher correctly reports `question` for interactive prompts (AskUserQuestion tool). This bug is specifically about detecting questions in free-text assistant output.

title: Agent metadata regressions: Codex detection + Claude rename/context + model persistence
description:
Track the current agent metadata work in `~/code/agents`.

Scope:
- Fix Codex pane detection (broken on macOS because process-name detection used truncated `ps -o comm` output)
- Persist and display active model for all agents
- Fix Claude regressions where `/rename` did not update dashboard title and `contextTokens/contextMax` were missing
- Fix Pi false idle/done reporting during active runs
- Add proper Codex hook-based reporting instead of scanner-only inference

Implemented / verified so far:
- Switched detection to use full process args instead of only `comm`, which fixes wrapped/vendor Codex binaries
- Added `model` persistence through `agents report` / state files and surfaced it in the UI
- Added `externalSessionId` to state so Claude pane sessions can map to Claude transcript JSONL files
- Scanner now resolves Claude renamed titles by reading the latest `/rename` `local_command` from `~/.claude/projects/.../<session>.jsonl`
- Added fallback inference for `contextTokens/contextMax` from pane footer content for Claude/Pi when state is missing them
- Fixed Pi extension state transitions in `extensions/pi/dustbot-reporting.ts`:
  - `turn_end` no longer reports `idle`
  - normal `tool_call` now reports `working`
  - `session_compact` now reports `working` instead of `idle`
  - only `agent_end` / `session_shutdown` should report idle
- Added Codex hook integration using Codex's documented `hooks.json` support:
  - new scripts in `extensions/codex/report-state.sh` and `extensions/codex/stop-hook.sh`
  - `agents setup` now patches `~/.codex/config.toml` to enable `[features] codex_hooks = true`
  - `agents setup` now merges our hook entries into `~/.codex/hooks.json`
  - fixed the installed `~/.codex/hooks.json` shape to the actual Codex format with a top-level `hooks` object; the earlier top-level event-key shape was ignored by Codex, which explained why no Codex state files were appearing
  - Codex hooks report `idle` on `SessionStart`, `working` on `UserPromptSubmit` / `PreToolUse(Bash)` / `PostToolUse(Bash)`, and `question` vs `idle` on `Stop`
  - Codex hook reports include `--model` and `--external-session-id`
- Scanner now uses a hybrid Codex detector:
  - hook-backed state for `working` / `idle` / `question`
  - generic content fallback retained for approval prompts
  - disabled Codex screen-scrape question fallback when there is no hook state, because it was falsely matching older `?` text in completed output
- Added Codex footer context inference from `XX% left` using `~/.codex/models_cache.json`, which now surfaces values like `contextTokens: 85272` and `contextMax: 258400`
- `npm test` passes
- `npm run build` passes
- `node dist/cli.js setup --quiet` fixed the live Codex config in `~/.codex/config.toml` and `~/.codex/hooks.json`

Current task / next verification:
- Need to validate the corrected Codex hook wiring against a real interactive Codex pane in tmux.
- Specifically check whether `~/.agents/state/codex-*.json` files are created/updated during interactive use and whether `agents ls` now reflects hook-driven `working` / `idle` transitions.

Key files:
- `src/scanner.ts`
- `src/state.ts`
- `src/cli.ts`
- `src/setup.ts`
- `extensions/claude/state-hook.sh`
- `extensions/claude/stop-hook.sh`
- `extensions/pi/dustbot-reporting.ts`
- `extensions/codex/report-state.sh`
- `extensions/codex/stop-hook.sh`
- `src/scanner.test.ts`
- `src/components/AgentTable.tsx`
- `src/components/Dashboard.tsx`
- `AGENTS.md`

Nuances / open follow-up:
- Already-running Claude panes need another hook event before `externalSessionId` lands in state and transcript-backed rename starts working
- Claude footer parsing currently yields display strings like `Opus 4.6 (1M context)` and approximate token counts from percentage/footer text
- Codex approval still relies on screen-scrape fallback because Codex hooks do not expose a dedicated approval event
- Quick local experiments suggested `codex exec` may not trigger hooks the same way as the interactive TUI; current implementation is aimed at interactive Codex panes, which is what `agents` monitors
- If interactive Codex still does not emit hook state, likely next places to inspect are Codex config-layer loading/trust and the exact runtime `hooks.json` shape expectations

title: Auto-create tmux session when launched outside tmux
description:
If `agents` is launched outside of a tmux session (no $TMUX env var), it should automatically:

1. Create a new tmux session (e.g. `tmux new-session -d -s agents`)
2. Launch `agents watch` inside that session
3. Attach to the session

This makes `agents` a single entry point — just type `agents` from any terminal and you get the dashboard in tmux, ready to create workspaces and monitor agents.

## Implementation

At the top of cli.ts, before command parsing:
- Check if `process.env.TMUX` is set
- If not, exec into `tmux new-session -s agents 'agents watch'` (or attach if session already exists)
- Use `execSync`/`execvp` style replacement so the original process is replaced

## Edge cases
- If a tmux `agents` session already exists, attach to it instead of creating a new one
- If tmux is not installed, print a helpful error
- Pass through any args: `agents ls` outside tmux should still just print and exit (only the dashboard needs tmux)

title: Launch profiles in config
Zellij: session-restorable agents workspaces
description:
The original cross-multiplexer umbrella is mostly delivered for tmux. The repository now has an `agents resurrect` integration, durable session/command metadata, tests, setup documentation, and the closed `bd-b0q.2` recovery slice. Keep this bead only for the remaining Zellij parity gap.

## Current gap

`createWorkspaceZellij()` creates a tab and starts the agent and helpers by injecting text with `write-chars`. It is not verified that native Zellij session restore can recover those commands, working directories, agent session identities, and helper layout after a server/process restart.

## Scope

- Verify the behavior in an isolated session on the currently supported stable Zellij version.
- If command injection is not restorable, use a Zellij-native layout/direct-launch path or durable agents metadata plus an explicit restore path.
- Preserve the workspace cwd, agent resume identity where available, helper commands, and supported layout semantics.
- Add focused automated tests where possible plus a documented real-session restore smoke.
- Keep tmux-resurrect behavior unchanged.

## Ownership boundary

This is an `agents` CLI/Zellij backend parity task. It does not own AgentsNext preview/adopt/exact-layout recovery, which lives in Shape item `item-1785235014239` and explicitly excludes Zellij from its first delivery.

## Acceptance criteria

- An isolated create, terminate, and restore scenario is documented and reproducible.
- The restored agent resumes the intended session when a stable external session id exists.
- Helper panes restart their intended commands rather than falling back silently to a shell.
- Cwd and the supported Zellij layout are preserved or any platform limitation is surfaced explicitly.
- Focused tests, the full test suite, and the build pass.
close_reason: Zellij is no longer a product priority

title: Detect sub-agent relationships in dashboard
description:
Detect when agents spawn background sub-agents and surface the relationship in the dashboard.

## Detection approaches

### Process tree (universal, no extension needed)
The scanner already walks process trees via findLeafProcess. Detect agent→agent parent-child chains (e.g. pi spawning claude). Tag these as sub-agents and show nested in dashboard.

### Pi extension hooks (richest data)
Pi's @tintinweb/pi-subagents provides Agent/get_subagent_result/steer_subagent tools. Hook into tool_call events to detect delegation:
```typescript
pi.on("tool_call", async (event) => {
  if (event.tool === "Agent") report("delegating");
});
```

### Claude
No tool-level hook events available. Fall back to process tree or screen-scrape for Agent tool patterns.

### Copilot
SDK sub-agent support unclear. Process tree fallback.

## Dashboard UX
- Show sub-agents as children of parent agent
- Parent status could show "delegating" or "working (2 sub-agents)"
- Clicking parent could expand/collapse sub-agent list

comments.author: peter
comments.text: Reconciliation 2026-08-13: Shape item-1776556887328 now owns the subagent hierarchy feature and has already selected the minimum upstream contract: a stable parentAgentID/parent reference in `agents ls --json`, with the first UI in the AgentsNext sidebar. The old bead mixes provider detection and dashboard/product UX. Create a narrow agents provider bead from the shaped contract when implementation is ready.

title: Make 'agents' default to dashboard, move list to 'agents ls'
description:
Currently `agents` (no subcommand) defaults to the interactive list picker (`agents list`). The dashboard (`agents watch`) is the primary UI and should be the default.

## Changes

- `agents` with no args → launch `agents watch` (dashboard)
- `agents ls` / `agents list` → current behavior (one-shot list, interactive picker)
- `agents watch` still works as explicit alias

In commander terms: change `isDefault: true` from the `list` command to the `watch` command.

title: Create agent from dashboard UI
description:
Add the ability to launch new agent workspaces directly from the dashboard without dropping to a shell.

## Proposed UX

**Trigger**: Press `n` (new) in the dashboard.

**Flow**:
1. A compact picker appears inline (replaces the hotkey bar), showing available launch profiles (see bd-1fw)
2. The picker header shows the inherited context: session name, cwd (shortened), and selected agent name — e.g. `dustbot ~/code/agents (claude)`
3. Navigate with j/k or arrow keys, confirm with Enter, cancel with Esc
4. On confirm: runs `agents ws <profile>` under the hood — creates a new tmux window with the agent + helper panes per the workspace layout config
5. The new agent appears in the dashboard list on the next scan refresh
6. Optionally auto-select and preview the new agent

**Minimal v1**: Skip the picker if there's only one profile — just launch it immediately on `n`.

## Context inheritance

The new workspace inherits from the currently selected agent in the list:
- **cwd**: Use the selected agent's pane working directory (`tmux display-message -t <paneId> -p '#{pane_current_path}'`)
- **tmux session/window**: Create the new window in the same tmux session as the selected agent

This is the natural UX — you're looking at an agent working on a project and want to spin up another one in the same context. If no agent is selected or the list is empty, fall back to the dashboard's own session and cwd.

## Edge cases
- If no profiles are configured, show a hint: "Configure launch profiles in ~/.agents/config.json"
- Dashboard stays focused in its own pane throughout (workspace creation happens in a new tmux window)

Depends on launch profiles (bd-1fw) being implemented first.

title: Zellij: break_panes_to_tab_with_index position/ID mismatch after tab deletion
description:
After a tab is deleted in Zellij 0.44, break_panes_to_tab_with_index validates by tab position but inserts by tab ID. These diverge after deletion, causing panes to land in wrong tabs or vanish entirely. This blocks side-by-side preview (swapping agent pane next to dashboard). Workaround: use break_panes_to_new_tab instead, but that creates a new tab every time rather than targeting an existing one.

Upstream: https://github.com/zellij-org/zellij/issues/3535 (open since Aug 2024, confirmed through 0.42.1+)
close_reason: Obsolete workaround tracker for an unsupported Zellij preview path

comments.author: peter
comments.text: Reconciliation 2026-08-13: current Zellij behavior intentionally uses tab-switch preview and disables side-by-side preview/grid, so this issue no longer blocks a supported path. The linked upstream issue #3535 remains open but has a 2026-07-01 report that PR #4685 fixed the tab-id/index problem in v0.44.0. If side-by-side Zellij preview returns, reproduce against current stable (v0.44.3 today) and create a fresh, evidence-scoped bead.

title: Zellij: resize_pane_with_id doesn't work on panes moved via break_panes_to_new_tab
description:
In Zellij 0.44, calling resize_pane_with_id on a pane that was moved via break_panes_to_new_tab has no effect. The plugin API resize silently fails. CLI resize (zellij action resize --pane-id) works as a workaround but requires a feedback loop (up to 30 iterations checking actual width) to achieve deterministic sizing. This blocks reliable side-by-side preview layout.

Upstream: NOT YET FILED — could not find an existing issue on zellij-org/zellij. Should file one with a minimal repro.
close_reason: Obsolete workaround tracker for an unsupported Zellij preview path

comments.text: Reconciliation 2026-08-13: current Zellij behavior intentionally uses tab-switch preview and disables side-by-side preview/grid; the resize workaround is not a supported product path and no upstream issue was ever filed. If side-by-side Zellij preview returns, reproduce on current stable and create a fresh bead with a minimal upstream repro rather than retaining the March 0.44 observation.

title: Harden pane ownership and resurrection
description:
Unify durable pane command identity with verified live runtime binding.

## Problem
Inherited TMUX_PANE can falsely classify ordinary terminals as agents, while real Commands panes can lose their executable across tmux-resurrect and return as zsh.

## Success Criteria
- Pane command identity and live runtime binding are separate concepts with one authoritative policy seam.
- Agent hooks cannot claim a pane from inherited environment alone.
- Commands panes restore their exact command and cwd after an isolated tmux restart.
- Stable pane identity rejects stale or mismatched bindings.
- Focused and full validation stay green.
close_reason: Both pane ownership and Commands resurrection reliability slices are implemented and validated

title: Reject unowned runtime reports from tmux panes
description:
Prevent embedded runtimes such as Shape Pi from using inherited TMUX_PANE as authoritative pane ownership.

## Evidence

## Success Criteria
- A report may mutate pane metadata only when the pane already has matching managed identity or a matching live foreground agent process.
- Unowned reports do not emit pane-scoped runtime state or change command metadata.
- Managed interactive agents continue to report state and update resumable launch metadata.
- Pi extension no longer writes tmux options directly.
- Regression tests cover embedded Pi, managed Pi, and stale shell metadata.

title: Restore Commands panes from durable desired-command metadata
description:
Make Commands-pane resurrection authoritative and testable across save and restore.

## Evidence
Before the 2026-08-09 reboot, agents windows 5 and 29 saved lazygit. After restore the same windows saved /bin/zsh --login and their sidecar command fields were empty.

## Success Criteria
- Every managed Commands pane persists command id, exact launch, cwd, and stable agents UUID.
- Snapshot and sidecar are treated as one validated generation; incomplete pairs do not replace the last good save.
- Restore resolves desired command by stable identity and verifies the executable is actually running.
- Failures are surfaced rather than silently accepted as zsh.
- An isolated tmux save, server restart, and restore test proves the behavior end to end.

title: Self-heal app-owned Kiro and Codex working-state bindings
description:
## Context

Working detection is currently missing for live AgentsNext panes even though their agent processes are running. This removes the white working shimmer in the UI. The custom pane background is not the primary cause; AgentsNext receives idle or missing runtime state.

Observed on 2026-08-13:
- Kiro pane %370: @agents_owned=app_owned, @agents_command_id=kiro, @agents_command_kind=agent, live kiro-cli descendant, but no kiro-%370 state/event.
- Codex pane %377: @agents_owned=app_owned and pane UUID, live codex descendant behind a zsh/wrapper foreground process, but command metadata and codex-%377 state/event are missing.
- Control pane %94: stale app-owned ordinary zsh terminal with no live agent. It must continue to reject inherited Pi reports.

## Root cause

The ownership hardening in bd-b0q.1 accepts either matching launcher provenance or a matching foreground agent. AgentsNext pane creation currently omits @agents_command_owner=launcher, while tmux pane_current_command often reports the wrapper shell rather than the live descendant agent. The scanner can find the descendant, but report binding does not use that evidence for legacy app-owned panes.

## Implementation scope

### agents repo

- Extend pane report metadata to read @agents_owned and the existing command launch.
- Keep launcher-owned matching command identity authoritative without requiring a live process.
- Add a narrowly scoped compatibility path for legacy app-owned panes: accept only when process-tree scanning finds a matching live descendant agent in the exact reported pane.
- Use that path to backfill launcher-owned command metadata on the first valid hook report.
- Preserve a more specific existing launch command during backfill instead of replacing it with only kiro or codex.
- Avoid process-tree scanning on the normal launcher-owned hook path.
- Keep stale app-owned shell panes and mismatched agents rejected.

Likely files: src/report-binding.ts, src/tmux-pane-metadata.ts, src/cli.ts and focused tests.

### agents-app repo

- In AgentsCore TMuxPaneCreationPlan.commandMetadataArguments, set @agents_command_owner to launcher for agent commands.
- In clearCommandMetadataArguments, explicitly clear @agents_command_owner when turning a pane into a terminal/web surface.
- Add focused Swift tests for both set and clear behavior.

Likely files: AgentsCore/Sources/AgentsCore/TMuxPaneCreationPlan.swift and AgentsCore/Tests/AgentsCoreTests/TMuxPaneCreationPlanTests.swift.

## Test-first repro

Before the agents fix, these should produce missing state:

printf userPromptSubmit | env TMUX_PANE=%370 AGENTS_HOME=<temp> extensions/kiro/report-state.sh
printf prompt | env TMUX_PANE=%377 AGENTS_HOME=<temp> extensions/codex/report-state.sh working

After the fix, both should produce pane-scoped working state because matching live descendants exist. The equivalent report for %94 must still be rejected.

## Acceptance criteria

- Fresh app-created agent panes contain @agents_command_owner=launcher.
- Existing ownerless app-owned Kiro/Codex panes self-heal on a valid hook report only when their matching live process is present.
- %370 and %377 report working and drive the AgentsNext shimmer while active.
- Custom pane background does not suppress the shimmer once working state is present.
- %94 and any app-owned shell without a matching live agent remain unchanged after a forged/inherited report.
- Resumable launch metadata remains specific and correct.
- Focused tests cover allowed legacy backfill, no-live rejection, wrong-agent rejection, owner set, and owner clear.
- Full TypeScript and AgentsCore/AgentsNext test suites pass.
- Install/relaunch the locally built AgentsNext and verify live tmux metadata plus agents ls --json.

## Handoff state

Work directly on main in both repositories and preserve unrelated dirt. The agents repo started clean and main was ahead of origin by 9 commits; relevant landed commits include ba21a01, e0cd44b, and 2365c85. No implementation edits for this bead have been made yet. The agents-app checkout had unrelated dirty scenario/docs work; stage only the intended AgentsCore source and test files. Previous baseline was 299 passing agents tests and 469 passing AgentsNext tests.
close_reason: Implemented and live-verified app-owned Kiro/Codex binding self-heal
